extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, applicants, and support staff using USPTO electronic filing and Internet communication channels
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO guidance on permitted/prohibited uses, formats, authentication, processing, and recordkeeping for electronic communications and filings (EFS-Web and related Patent Electronic System). Covers what may be filed, how documents are processed/stored, user/registration rules, fees, and interview/video conferencing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email submissions not accepted as adequate replies to Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to an Office action is improperly submitted by applicant via email, the email submission will not be accepted as an adequate reply to avoid abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A printed copy of email communications MUST be entered into One Patent Service Gateway (via Patent Data Portal) and entered in the patent application file (Doc Code is EMAIL). A copy of the email submission will be placed in the application file with an indication that the reply is NOT ENTERED.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO employees may not initiate email communications without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees are NOT permitted to initiate communications with applicants via email unless there is a written authorization of record in the patent application by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization of Internet communications allows USPTO employees to respond to email and initiate communications. For reissue applications and reexamination patentees, written authorization by the applicant or patentee is required before USPTO employees may initiate email communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication requirement for sender by patent organization recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Email must be initiated by a registered practitioner, or an applicant in a pro se application, and sufficient information must be provided to show representative capacity in compliance with 37 CFR 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of identifying information include attorney registration number, attorney docket number, and patent application number. Examiners should verify identity (e.g., check Patent Data Portal or the application file and previously provided email addresses) and should not disclose information until identity is adequately verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate response channels after receiving applicant email
rubrics_metrics.description: Once email correspondence has been received from the applicant as set forth in Patent Internet Usage Policy Article 4, such correspondence must be responded to appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Examiner may respond to an applicant’s email correspondence by telephone, fax, or other appropriate means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using email/instant messaging for interview exchanges without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Email and instant messaging shall NOT be used to conduct an exchange of communications similar to those exchanged during telephone or personal interviews unless a written authorization has been given under Patent Internet Usage Policy Article 5 to use Internet email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorized, a paper copy of the Internet email or instant messaging contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file (as required by the Federal Records Act), analogous to entering an Examiner Interview Summary Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video conferencing use and hosting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO video conferencing tools may be used to conduct examiner interviews in both published and unpublished applications under the Patent Internet Usage Policy, but authorization by the practitioner is required prior to sending an official USPTO communication link or tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video conferencing must be made using USPTO tools and hosted by USPTO personnel. All interviews by video conference must originate from USPTO links provided by the examiner; links provided by the applicant from non‑USPTO tools are not acceptable. No personal phones, email, PDAs, etc. may be used by USPTO employees for Official communications. Practitioner participation is considered consent to use the tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate copies of correspondence policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Since each file must be complete in itself, a separate copy of every paper to be filed in a patent, patent file, or other proceeding must be furnished for each file to which the paper pertains, even though the contents may be identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing duplicate copies should be avoided except where Office requires duplicate copies. The Office may dispose of or discard duplicate copies and filing duplicates may cause processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS‑Web file format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All EFS-Web submissions are required to be in PDF unless otherwise indicated in this framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted non‑PDF formats include: (1) ASCII plain text (.TXT) for nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings, computer program listings, mega tables, and Complex Work Units; (2) zip compressed files to submit request forms generated by PCT‑SAFE or ePCT for international applications; and (3) JPEG files for drawings in international design applications. Users need not provide duplicate copies of documents filed through EFS‑Web unless specifically required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and advantage of EFS‑Web fillable and web-based forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO provides EFS‑Web-fillable PDF forms (e.g., Provisional Application Cover Sheet, IDS, ADS, Petition to Make Special, RCE Transmittal). When users submit information using an EFS‑Web‑fillable form (not a scanned image), the information will directly load into USPTO databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other USPTO-created PDF fillable forms are available on the USPTO website. Information on non‑EFS‑Web-fillable forms will not auto-load. Web-based ePetitions, Requests for Withdrawal, and eTerminal Disclaimers can be filled completely online and are auto‑processed and immediately granted or approved if they meet all requirements; if not, they will not be loaded into IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered versus unregistered user filing capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered users may file follow-on documents via EFS‑Web and file more types of submissions; unregistered users can file most patent applications via EFS‑Web but are limited in the follow‑on documents they may file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unregistered users cannot file follow-on documents after initial submission except limited ePetitions (e.g., make special based on age, accept unintentionally delayed maintenance fee). Registered users may file copies for publication, follow-on documents including amendments, IDS, replies to Office actions, evidence, petitions, and terminal disclaimers. No user may file papers in an application or proceeding if not a practitioner of record or acting in representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.32 and 1.34, except as expressly authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and conspicuous identification requirements for follow‑on documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in an application must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33(b) and must identify on the top page in a conspicuous location the application number (series code and serial number), the serial number and filing date assigned, or the international application/registration number as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.4, 1.5, and 1.33(b) for formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent applications and documents permitted via EFS‑Web
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS‑Web permits registered and unregistered users to file a wide range of application types and documents via its web interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted filings include: (1) Provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(b); (2) Nonprovisional utility applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (including Track One/accelerated requests on initial filing); (3) Nonprovisional design applications (35 U.S.C. 171); (4) PCT international applications filed in the U.S. Receiving Office (35 U.S.C. 361); (5) Submissions to enter national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371; (6) International design applications under the Hague Agreement; (7) Requests for ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302 as new submissions; (8) Requests for supplemental examination under 35 U.S.C. 257 as new submissions; (9) Third‑Party Preissuance Submissions under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290 via a dedicated interface; (10) Citation of prior art and written statements under 37 CFR 1.501 via a dedicated interface; (11) Petitions to make special based on age under 37 CFR 1.102(c); (12) Petitions to accept unintentionally delayed maintenance fee payments under 37 CFR 1.378 (and payments when submitted with the petition); (13) Reissue utility and design patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent applications and documents NOT permitted via EFS‑Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain submissions cannot be filed using EFS‑Web and are explicitly disallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited submissions include (non‑exhaustive): (1) Plant patent applications and associated follow-on documents (except certain third‑party submissions); (2) Reexamination requests for plant patents; (3) Third party inquiries/papers unless authorized by the framework and filed via the correct EFS‑Web interface; (4) Initial submissions for patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 156; (5) Correspondence concerning registration to practice (37 CFR 1.4(e)); (6) Certified documents (37 CFR 1.4(f)); (7) Certified copies of priority documents (37 CFR 1.55); (8) Correspondence for secrecy-ordered applications (37 CFR 5.1–5.5); (9–10) Documents for contested PTAB cases/trials (file via PTAB End to End); (11) Disciplinary proceeding correspondence (37 CFR part 11); (12) Maintenance fees not submitted with a petition under 37 CFR 1.378; (13) Assignment documents (file via EPAS); (14) Submissions not associated with a patent/application/reexamination/supplemental exam; (15) Court appeal notices/complaints. If such documents are submitted via EFS‑Web they will not be accorded a date of receipt or considered officially filed, and no benefit will be given to a certificate of transmission under 37 CFR 1.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auto‑processed ePetitions and web‑based documents
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS‑Web permits registered users to file certain auto‑processed ePetitions, requests, and eTerminal Disclaimers which will be auto‑processed and granted or approved immediately if they meet all requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples auto‑processed for registered users: request for withdrawal as attorney or agent; petition to withdraw an application from issue under 37 CFR 1.313 (with restrictions); petition for revival under 37 CFR 1.137 (with restrictions); eTerminal Disclaimers for nonprovisional utility applications under 37 CFR 1.321(b) and (c); petition to correct assignee after payment of issue fee under 37 CFR 3.81(b). Auto‑processed ePetitions for registered and unregistered users include petition to make special based on age (37 CFR 1.102) and petition to accept unintentionally delayed maintenance fee payment (37 CFR 1.378(b)). If an ePetition does not meet all formal requirements it will not be accepted or loaded into IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official record conversion and storage for EFS‑Web submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When USPTO successfully receives PDF documents via EFS‑Web, the PDFs will be converted into TIFF image files and stored in the Image File Wrapper (IFW) as part of the official record; certain drawings and ASCII text documents are stored in SCORE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official record comprises: (1) ASCII text documents and drawings stored in SCORE (e.g., sequence listings, program listings); (2) TIFF images of all other original documents stored in IFW; (3) The Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt and the Electronic Patent Application Fee Transmittal containing GUI data; (4) TIFF images in IFW for international design applications generated from XML received from the International Bureau. Some pre‑grant publication submissions are forwarded to the Pre‑Grant Publication Division and are not stored in IFW/SCORE as part of the official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of internally inconsistent information submitted via EFS‑Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Routing of the submission to the appropriate Office area is based on the application type indicated in EFS‑Web; conflicting indications may cause routing based on the EFS‑Web selection and may require a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other conflicts, applicable regulations resolve the conflict (e.g., inventorship determined under 37 CFR 1.41). If no correspondence information is included or not in compliance, the Office may use application data furnished through EFS‑Web (e.g., customer number-associated address) for correspondence until corrected by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size equivalency for application size fee purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of the paper size equivalent for applications filed via EFS‑Web for application size fee purposes follows 37 CFR 1.52(f)(2) and MPEP § 607.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper size equivalency under 37 CFR 1.52(f)(2) for EFS‑Web filings does not apply to the application size fee under 37 CFR 1.492(j) for national stage submissions under 35 U.S.C. 371. See MPEP § 1893.01(c) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and timing of fee payments via EFS‑Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Both unregistered and registered users may submit filing fees (basic filing, search, examination, excess claims) using the online fee payment in EFS‑Web at the time of filing; only registered users may submit payment of fees in a previously filed application or proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS‑Web permits payment by credit/debit card, USPTO deposit account, or electronic fund transfer. Users should NOT submit credit/debit card charge authorization forms electronically via EFS‑Web (e.g., PTO‑2038) because such information would be entered into the application file; instead submit such transmittals by facsimile to USPTO Central Facsimile or by Priority Mail Express per 37 CFR 1.10. Failure to timely pay certain fees (e.g., basic national fee for national stage) results in abandonment. To avoid a surcharge for filing‑date payments, fees must be submitted and received by USPTO before midnight ET on the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions that cannot be filed when online fee payment is unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: When the online fee payment in EFS‑Web is unavailable, certain submission types cannot be filed via EFS‑Web because online fee payment must accompany the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These include: (1) Petitions that require a fee for auto‑processing by EFS‑Web; (2) Pre‑grant publication submissions under 37 CFR 1.211–1.221 that require a fee; (3) Third‑party preissuance submissions under 37 CFR 1.290 that require a fee; (4) Web‑based Issue Fee Payment (Web 85b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt as official date of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt establishes the date of receipt by the USPTO of documents submitted via EFS‑Web and contains a full listing of documents submitted as described by the user, including count of pages and/or byte sizes for each document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt is the electronic equivalent of the postcard receipt (MPEP § 503). The official application filing date will be noted on the filing receipt after submitted application parts are reviewed for compliance (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 111 or 35 U.S.C. 371). Filing dates for reexamination and supplemental examination are similarly based on review and the date indicated on the Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for lost/damaged/unreadable official versions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the official version of any document received by EFS‑Web is lost, damaged, or rendered unreadable and cannot be recovered from stored files, the user will be promptly notified and may need to resubmit and petition for the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To seek restoration of the original filing date the user must present: (1) the Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt; (2) a copy of the missing files as submitted; and (3) a signed petition accompanied by a statement that the attached files are the same as those originally submitted (e.g., petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) or 1.182 with appropriate fee).
